title: Second moment of the Rademacher distribution
statement:
Let $\mathrm{Rad} = \tfrac{1}{2}\delta_{-1} + \tfrac{1}{2}\delta_{+1}$ be the Rademacher distribution on $\bbr$, placing equal mass $1/2$ at $-1$ and at $+1$. Then its second moment equals one:
\[
\int_{\bbr} y^2 \, d\mathrm{Rad}(y) = 1.
\]
hypotheses_covered: integrand is the square function $y \mapsto y^2$
replaced:
The second moment of the Rademacher distribution equals one:
$\int y^2 \, d\mathrm{Rad}(y) = 1$.
